Migrating from dMod

Source: vignettes/articles/migrating.Rmd
migrating.Rmd

What a dMod [1] script has to change for dMod2.

Unchanged interface

Function objects and algebra are the same: Xs(), Xf(), Y(), P(), Pexpl(), Pimpl(), normL2(), constraintL2(), datapointL2(), with * for concatenation, + for conditions or objective terms, and normL2(data, g * x * p). eqnlist(), addReaction(), define(), insert(), branch(), repar(), trust(), mstrust(), profile() and plot*() keep names and main arguments. dMod2 has getSymbols() and replaceSymbols(), so library(cOde) is not needed.

Substitution syntax

define(), insert(), repar() and branch(apply = ) take "lhs <- rhs"; "lhs ~ rhs" is an error naming the new form.

dMod dMod2
define(trafo, "x ~ x", x = pars) define(trafo, "x <- x", x = pars)
insert(trafo, "x ~ exp(x)", x = pars) insert(trafo, "x <- exp(x)", x = pars)
insert(trafo, "x ~ x*x_OE", dose == 10, ...) insert(trafo, "x <- x*x_OE", dose == 10, ...)

Placeholders in ..., branch table columns in scope, unnamed logical condition selectors and conditionMatch are unchanged.

~ now writes effect formulas: on a branched transformation, insert() takes an unquoted formula and replaces the symbol by a linear predictor over the branch table columns, fixed and random effects in lme4 notation:

trafo <- branch(trafo, table = covariates)        # one row per condition, columns ID and wt
trafo <- insert(trafo, "x <- exp(x)", x = c("ka", "cl"))
trafo <- insert(trafo, x ~ 1 + (1 | ID), x = c("ka", "cl"))
trafo <- insert(trafo, v ~ wt + (1 | gr(ID, dist = spikeSlab())))
randomEffects(trafo)

See Sparse deviations and Nonlinear mixed-effects models.

Backend and compilation

The default odemodel(backend = "cppDE") generates C++ code through cppDE; "Sundials" runs CVODES through cppDE::cvode(), "deSolve" keeps the dMod path with code compiled by cOde.

Every function object is compiled. With compile = FALSE only sources are written, and one compile() builds them into one shared object:

dMod

x <- Xs(odemodel(r, modelname = "x"))
g <- Y(obs, r, attach.input = FALSE)
p <- P(trafo, condition = "C1")

dMod2

x <- Xs(odemodel(r, modelname = "x", compile = FALSE))
g <- Y(obs, x, modelname = "g", compile = FALSE)
p <- P(trafo, condition = "C1", modelname = "p", compile = FALSE)
compile(x, g, p, output = "model")

Files go to outdir, default getOption("dMod2.outdir"), else the working directory.

dMod dMod2
odemodel(solver = ) odemodel(backend = c("cppDE", "Sundials", "deSolve"))
odemodel(outputs = , estimate = , gridpoints = ) ..., deSolve only
Xs(optionsOde = , optionsSens = ) Xs(options = , optionsSens = ), see cppDE::solveODE()
Xs(fcontrol = ) deSolve only
none deriv2 = TRUE in odemodel(), Y(), P(): exact second derivatives

Renamed arguments

Dotted argument names are lowerCamelCase.

dMod dMod2 in
attach.input attachInput Y(), Pexpl()
keep.root keepRoot Pimpl()
attr.name attrName normL2(), constraintL2(), datapointL2()
split.by, keep.covariates splitBy, keepCovariates as.datalist()
sort.by sortBy as.parframe() of a parlist
obj.attributes objAttributes parframe()
studyname name, default "mstrust" mstrust()
value parameter datapointL2()
nameFlux legendTitle plotFluxes()
atr which attrs()
S (stoichiometric matrix) eqnlist conservedQuantities()

Optimization

trust() drops parscale, fterm, mterm; thresholds go to tolControl, step settings to stepControl.

dMod dMod2
trust(..., fterm = , mterm = ) trust(..., tolControl = list(ftol = , mtol = , gtol = ))
trust(parscale = ) removed
Gauss-Newton Hessian only hessianMethod = c("gn", "bfgs", "sr1", "exact")
mstrust(..., studyname = "fits") mstrust(..., name = "fits", resultPath = ".")
mstrust(cores = ) cores = n, or c(fits = , conditions = )

Profile likelihood

profile(obj, pars, whichPar) keeps method, stepControl, algoControl and defaults. Changes:

dMod dMod2
optControl = list(fterm = , mterm = ) any trust() argument, e.g. tolControl
stepControl = list(stop = "data") stop: also any numeric attribute of the objective
threshold qchisq(1 - alpha, 1) delta =, e.g. profileThreshold(method = "F", n = , p = )
both sides side = c("both", "left", "right")
algoControl = list(W = "hessian"): Gauss-Newton exact Hessian with deriv2 = TRUE
cores = over parameters cores = n, or c(pars = , conditions = )
none attribute "ends": steps and stop reason per side
none sparse = "auto": sparse Hessian where available

confint() uses the data term by default, val.column = "value" the whole objective; see Profile likelihood for the method. Stop reasons in "ends" are threshold, limit, step limit or error.

Steady states

Pimpl() solves by pseudo-transient continuation in C++ instead of rootSolve::multiroot(). On an eqnlist, flow = TRUE (default) returns the stable steady state reached by the flow; settings such as positive go to controlsPTC. P(eqnlist) without method is implicit, steadyStates() derives an analytic transformation.

Removed functions

dMod dMod2
priorL2(mu, lambda) constraintL2(mu, sigma)
nll() normL2(optBLOQ = c("M3", "M1", "M4NM", "M4BEAL"))
mname() modelname()
funC0() cppDE::cppFUN()
ginv() MASS::ginv()
wide2long(prediction) as.data.frame(prediction)

Changed defaults

These run without error but give results different from dMod.

  • odemodel(): cppDE (BDF) instead of deSolve lsoda; trajectories differ within tolerances.
  • Y(): attachInput = FALSE, g * x returns observables only.
  • P(): an eqnlist as trafo gives an implicit transformation.
  • trust(): iterlim = 1000 instead of 100, tolControl with ftol = mtol = gtol = 1e-6; mstrust() passes both on.
  • mstrust(): retry = TRUE restarts a fit that errors, up to nTries = 10 attempts.
  • compile(): cores = detectFreeCores() instead of 1.
  • confint(): val.column = "data" instead of "value", a prior no longer narrows the interval.
  • fitErrorModel(): plotting = FALSE.
